blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Adjectives are small words. But they tell you a lot. A late delivery, a heavy truck, a safe driver — you know the story in half a sentence.

Adjectives come before the noun. We say a fast truck, not a truck fast. They do not change form. We say a good man and a good woman. Both are "good".

Use adjectives, but not too many. "Very" adds strength: very late. "A bit" makes it softer: a bit late. Clear adjectives help the team make faster decisions.

items.q: Where do adjectives go in English?
options: At the end of the sentence
items.why: "Adjectives come before the noun." — a fast truck.

items.q: Do adjectives change form for a man or a woman?
items.why: "They do not change form. good man and good woman."

items.q: What does the word "very" do?
items.why: "'Very' adds strength: very late."

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE with which idea?
options: You should use many adjectives in one sentence.
One clear adjective can save a long explanation.
Adjectives are not important at work.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que adjetivos contam a história "in half a sentence" e ajudam decisões rápidas.

items.q: Which sentence is softer?
options: The truck is a bit late.
items.why: Inferência: "'A bit' makes it softer: a bit late." — "very" é mais forte.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry falando com Emily sobre os motoristas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi Emily. Let me tell you about the drivers this morning. It was a busy day, and the road was full of traffic.

Tom was on time. He is a safe driver. He is not fast — he is a bit slow — but he is very careful. His truck was full and heavy, and he still arrived on time. Good work.

Sara was a bit late, only ten minutes. The road was busy this morning and there was a lot of traffic. It was not her fault, so that is fine.

Then there is Mark. Mark was very late. One hour late! His truck was empty, so it was light and fast. But he stopped for a long coffee on the way. That is the real problem, not the road. The road was clear for him.

So, two good drivers and one small problem. Tom and Sara are fine. I will have a quiet word with Mark tomorrow. You know me, Emily — I like clear, simple words. A safe driver is worth more than a fast one. On time is good. Safe and on time is better.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Was Tom on time or late?
items.why: "Tom was on time. He is a safe driver."

items.q: Why was Sara a bit late?
options: The road was busy with traffic
items.why: "Sara was a bit late... The road was busy this morning and there was a lot of traffic."

items.q: Why was Mark very late?
options: He stopped for a long coffee
items.why: "But he stopped for a long coffee on the way. That is the real problem."

items.q: Which driver does Harry respect the most?
options: Tom, because he is safe and on time
Mark, because his truck is fast
items.why: Inferência: Harry diz "A safe driver is worth more than a fast one" e elogia o Tom.

items.q: Whose lateness is Harry NOT worried about?
items.why: Inferência: da Sara — "It was not her fault, so that is fine." Ele só vai falar com o Mark.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "This truck is very fast on the motorway." Fast means…
items.why: Fast = rápido, alta velocidade.

items.q: "Traffic is bad, so the van is very slow today." Slow means…
items.why: Slow = lento, o oposto de fast.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good driver is a ___ driver — no accidents."
items.why: Safe = seguro; um motorista sem acidentes é safe.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The road is very ___ this morning, full of cars."
items.why: Busy = movimentado; cheio de carros.

items.q: "The truck came back empty after the delivery." Empty means…
items.why: Empty = vazio, sem nada dentro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem no trabalho de entregas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The van will drop off the boxes at nine." To drop off means to…
items.why: Drop off = deixar / entregar algo em um lugar.

items.q: "We need to pick up the goods from the warehouse." To pick up means to…
items.why: Pick up = pegar / coletar algo.

items.q: "Sorry, I am going to run late today." To run late means to…
items.why: Run late = estar / chegar atrasado.

items.q: "The traffic will hold up the delivery." To hold up means to…
items.why: Hold up = atrasar, segurar.

items.q: "Please deliver the parcel on time." On time means…
options: at the right time, not late
items.why: On time = no horário, nem atrasado nem adiantado.
